profiles.meeting_scenario: The county is preparing an MCDA-based decision process for a former wood-treatment site contaminated with creosote, arsenic, and PAHs near a riverfront redevelopment area. An internal planning meeting is being held to organize the first decision-framing workshop, where technical staff and a community advisory group will review remedial alternatives, criteria, and the information package that will support later ranking. The agenda is to confirm what materials need to be prepared, how stakeholder input will be gathered, who owns each piece, and the timeline leading up to the workshop. The expected outcome is an apparently shared plan for producing the workshop packet, assembling the risk and cost inputs, and structuring the MCDA exercise.

members.name: Lena Ortiz
members.role: Remedial Project Manager and Human Health Risk Lead
members.expertise: contaminated site risk assessment, feasibility studies, regulatory remedy selection
members.background: Lena works for the county's environmental remediation unit and has managed several brownfield cleanups through risk assessment, remedy screening, and regulator review. She is used to internal technical meetings where terms like 'alternatives,' 'baseline risk,' and 'criteria definitions' refer to artifacts already standardized in feasibility-study work.
members.private_state: Lena wants the MCDA workshop to stay tightly bounded so the team can move toward a preferred remedy without reopening earlier technical screening decisions. She is concerned about schedule slippage and about presenting anything that looks too provisional to regulators.
hidden_assumptions: When the team says 'shortlisted alternatives,' it naturally means the three remedy families already retained after engineering screening in the feasibility study.
The 'baseline risk numbers' for planning are the February 2024 revised industrial-use tables from the current risk memo, because internal work should always use the latest approved technical draft.
Finalizing 'criteria definitions' means locking concise technical descriptors and source tables for the MCDA model, not building public-facing explanatory content.
Getting 'weights from the advisory group' means collecting directional preference signals that staff can translate into model inputs afterward; a lightweight elicitation is sufficient at this stage.

members.name: Evan Cho
members.role: Decision Analyst and Stakeholder Engagement Specialist
members.expertise: MCDA design, workshop facilitation, public-sector decision processes
members.background: Evan is an external consultant brought in to structure the MCDA process and facilitate the advisory group. He has worked on infrastructure and environmental planning projects where the decision process must be legible to nontechnical stakeholders and where workshop materials are designed around what participants have already seen publicly.
members.private_state: Evan wants the workshop to generate stakeholder input that can be used directly in the MCDA record, demonstrating that the process was transparent and not merely consultative. He is concerned that if materials are too technical or if options seem pre-filtered, the advisory group will feel managed rather than involved.
hidden_assumptions: When people say 'shortlisted alternatives,' they mean the stakeholder-facing set of options to be compared in the workshop, typically framed as complete remedy-use packages rather than engineering families alone.

The 'baseline risk numbers' to anchor discussion should match the 2022 public fact sheet and prior community materials, because continuity matters more than internal draft updates in a facilitated setting.
Finalizing 'criteria definitions' includes plain-language explanations, examples, and prompts so nontechnical participants can score and discuss the criteria consistently.

Getting 'weights from the advisory group' means conducting a formal elicitation that produces normalized weights directly traceable to participants' judgments, not just gathering informal preference signals.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the shortlisted alternatives
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree to prepare the 'shortlist of alternatives' for the workshop.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the three remedy families already retained after technical screening: excavation/off-site disposal, cap with institutional controls, and in-situ stabilization with targeted hot-spot removal.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means three stakeholder-facing comparison packages that bundle remedy approach with future land-use posture and access assumptions, such as 'industrial containment,' 'mixed-use hot-spot removal,' and 'riverfront restoration emphasis.'
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both treat 'shortlist' as an obvious carryover from earlier work, and each hears the other as merely endorsing a standard next step rather than specifying the level of option granularity.

misalignment_points.topic: Which baseline risk numbers will anchor the MCDA packet
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to using the 'baseline risk numbers' in the comparison tables.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the February 2024 revised HHRA tables for the current industrial receptor scenario, which have not yet been shown outside the project team.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the 2022 community fact sheet values tied to the mixed-use future scenario discussed in prior public meetings.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase sounds precise enough that neither expects ambiguity, and both versions are legitimate documents associated with the same site, so the mismatch hides behind a shared label.

misalignment_points.topic: What is included in finalizing criteria definitions
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree that Evan will help 'finalize the criteria definitions' before the workshop packet goes out.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes this means tightening the technical wording of criteria, units, and data sources in the internal MCDA matrix, such as how 'implementability' and 'residual risk' are labeled.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes it also includes converting each criterion into plain-language text, adding examples, and drafting the short discussion prompts participants will see in the packet.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In many projects 'criteria definitions' naturally refers to the whole supporting write-up, but in technical teams it often refers only to the model-ready column definitions; both uses are routine and sound interchangeable in a planning conversation.

misalignment_points.topic: How stakeholder weights will be obtained
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both say they will 'get the weights from the advisory group' during the workshop.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 expects a quick sticker-dot or ranking exercise that reveals rough relative importance, after which staff will regularize the weights for the MCDA model.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 expects a structured swing-weighting exercise with anchor ranges and live normalization so the elicited values can be entered directly into the model as stakeholder-derived weights.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: They agree on the outcome in broad terms and each assumes the method is the standard one for their own practice, so neither feels a need to spell out the mechanics in an initial planning discussion.

When I say the shortlisted alternatives, I mean the three remedy families already retained after screening. If we keep the packet tight and technical enough, we can stay on schedule and avoid giving regulators something that looks half-baked.
